notes.deenhindi-nasai:2687: Both complete originals read. Aisha supplies perfuming at entering ihram and for ending it after the Jamrat-al-Aqabah stoning but before the House tawaf. All three temporal relations remain exactly as printed. No timing is borrowed from the neighbouring shorter versions.
notes.deenhindi-nasai:2688: Both complete originals read. Preserve Aisha's supplied perfuming for ending and entering ihram and the actual comparison that it was unlike the addressees' perfume. The appended expressly marked yani explanation that it was not long-lasting is an unassigned interpretive explanation of that comparison; keep its exact words as source context rather than silently attributing the gloss to Aisha or inventing a separate event. The body retains the comparison itself.
notes.deenhindi-nasai:2690: Both complete originals read. Aisha supplies her own habitual application of the best perfume she could obtain at the addressee's entering ihram. This short field uses the honorific recipient pronoun but does not itself name the Messenger; preserve that pronominal attribution and do not fill the name from surrounding occurrences. The availability limitation and habitual action remain complete.
notes.deenhindi-nasai:2691: Both complete originals read. Urdu explicitly gives Aisha's application of the best obtainable perfume at entering/ending ihram and intended House visit. Hindi truncates the main application action and the best-perfume phrase, but supplies the named recipient and the temporal/intention clauses. Keep its own abbreviated fragment with the missing main action disclosed; do not add perfume, quality or a final predicate from Urdu.
